meta.name: Notify on workflow errors via Slack with Discord fallback

name: Notify Slack on workflow errors, with a Discord fallback

parameters.content:
## Error notifier with dedup and a fallback channel

Attach this workflow as the "Error Workflow" (Settings → Error Workflow) on any of your other n8n workflows. When one of them fails, this workflow receives the error via n8n's built-in Error Trigger, skips duplicate notifications for the same execution, and posts a readable summary to Slack. If the Slack post itself fails (bad URL, Slack outage, etc.), it automatically falls back to Discord instead of failing silently.

### Before you activate
1. Create a Slack Incoming Webhook (no Slack app/OAuth needed) and paste its URL into the "Set: Slack webhook URL" node.
2. Create a Discord Incoming Webhook (Channel Settings → Integrations → Webhooks) and paste its URL into the "Set: Discord webhook URL" node.
3. Activate this workflow, then open the workflow(s) you want monitored → Settings → Error Workflow → select this workflow.

### Note on deduplication
Deduplication uses n8n's workflow static data, which is only persisted for executions triggered automatically (not manual test runs) — this is expected and matches how Error Workflows actually run in production.

Step 1 — Detect & de-duplicate

Receives the error from n8n's Error Trigger, extracts the workflow name, failing node, error message and execution URL, and checks whether this exact execution was already notified (skips repeat notifications from multi-failure scenarios).

Step 2 — Notify Slack

Posts a formatted error summary to Slack via an Incoming Webhook. If the request fails for any reason, control passes to the fallback step instead of the notification being silently lost.

Step 3 — Fallback to Discord

Only runs if the Slack notification failed. Posts the same error summary to a Discord channel via an Incoming Webhook, so a broken Slack integration never means you hear nothing about a failure.

nodes.name: Check duplicate & summarize error
nodes.notes: Uses $getWorkflowStaticData('global') to remember which execution IDs have already been notified. Static data only persists for automatically-triggered executions (not manual test runs) — confirmed against docs.n8n.io, 2026-08-12. That's fine here since Error Workflows only ever run automatically in real use.

Set: Slack webhook URL
nodes.notes: Placeholder value — not a real webhook URL. Create your own Slack Incoming Webhook and paste the URL here before activating.

nodes.name: Slack notify succeeded?
nodes.notes: Checks the actual response body, not just the absence of a thrown error. Slack's Incoming Webhook returns the literal text "ok" on success (confirmed via a real test send, 2026-08-12). An invalid/malformed webhook URL does NOT reliably produce an HTTP error — it can redirect to Slack's own developer docs page (HTTP 200, HTML body), which a check that only looks for $json.error would wrongly treat as success. This was an actual bug found during testing.

nodes.name: Set: Discord webhook URL
nodes.notes: Placeholder value — not a real webhook URL. In Discord: Channel Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL, then paste it here before activating.

nodes.name: Notify Discord (fallback)
nodes.notes: If this also fails, the execution list in n8n itself remains the last resort record of the failure — there is no further fallback beyond Discord in this template.
